en.name: Sunflower seeds, roasted and salted, in the shell
en.summary: There is no fixed timeline for roasted, salted sunflower seeds in the shell: the honest answer is to go by the use-by date printed on the pack. What the record does say is that roasted seeds will become rancid if they are kept at room temperature for long periods, so the date is a real limit rather than a formality.
en.pantry: Store them sealed, cool, dark and dry, and use the printed use-by date as your limit — no separate shelf-life figure is published for this form, and inventing one would not help you. The reason the date matters is that these seeds have been roasted, and roasting heats the oil and starts the oxidation that eventually makes them taste bitter. The salt adds a second problem: it draws moisture out of a humid kitchen, so a half-open bag goes soft and the shells turn chewy well before the seeds turn.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for this form either. Cold storage is not wrong — the failure here is oxidation, and low temperature slows it, which is why it helps other roasted seeds — but there is no published figure for in-shell salted seeds, so the printed date remains your guide. If you do chill a large bag, seal it properly and let it warm before opening so the shells do not take up condensation.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline exists for these. Freezing would not damage them, since there is very little water in a sunflower seed, but with no published figure and a use-by date on the pack there is nothing to be gained by it. Buy in the size you will finish, which is the practical answer for a snack eaten by the handful.
en.thawing: Not applicable in normal use. If a bag has been kept cold, let it return to room temperature sealed before opening.
spoilage: A bitter, sharp kernel when you crack a few shells — rancid oil.
Shells that have gone soft and chewy, from salt pulling in moisture.
A smell of old cooking oil rather than something toasted and salty.
Mould or a musty smell in a bag that got genuinely damp.
tips: Look for the use-by date on the pack before buying; it is the only timeline you have.
Clip an opened bag or decant into an airtight tub; salt makes them soften fast.
Keep them out of the sun and away from the hob.
Crack a few from different parts of the bag before serving a bowlful.

faq.q: How long do salted sunflower seeds in the shell keep?
faq.a: No fixed timeline is published. Go by the use-by date on the pack, and store them sealed in a cool, dry, dark place.

faq.q: Do in-shell sunflower seeds go rancid?
faq.a: Yes. Roasted seeds will become rancid if kept at room temperature for long periods, which is why the printed date is worth taking seriously.

faq.q: Why have my sunflower seeds gone soft?
faq.a: The salt on the shells pulls moisture out of humid air. Reseal the bag properly, or move the seeds into an airtight tub.

zh.name: 帶殼烤鹹葵瓜子
zh.summary: 帶殼的烤鹹葵瓜子沒有固定的保存期限數字：老實的答案是看包裝上標示的有效日期。資料另外說明的是，烤過的種子如果長時間放在室溫下會油耗，所以那個日期是實質的限制，不是形式。
zh.pantry: 密封、陰涼、避光、乾燥存放，並以包裝上的有效日期為限——這個形式沒有另外公布的保存期限數字，硬給一個也幫不上你。日期之所以重要，是因為這些種子被烘烤過，而烘烤加熱了油脂、啟動了最後會讓它發苦的氧化。鹽又帶來第二個問題：它會把濕熱廚房裡的水氣吸過來，所以一包開了一半的瓜子，常常在種仁走味之前，殼就先軟掉、變得韌韌的了。
zh.fridge: 這個形式同樣沒有公布的冷藏期限。低溫保存不算錯——這裡的失效是氧化，而低溫會拖慢它，這也是它對其他烤過的種子有用的原因——但帶殼鹹瓜子沒有公開數字，所以還是以包裝日期為準。真要冰一大包，請確實密封，並且回溫後再打開，免得殼吸到結露。
zh.freezer: 這項沒有冷凍的期限數據。冷凍不會傷到它，因為葵瓜子含水極少；但既然沒有公開數字、包裝上又有有效日期，冷凍就沒什麼好賺的。實際的答案是：買你吃得完的份量——這本來就是一把一把嗑掉的零食。
zh.thawing: 一般用不到。若冰過，請維持密封回到室溫再打開。
spoilage: 剝幾顆嚐種仁，發苦而尖銳——那是油耗。
殼變軟變韌，那是鹽把水氣吸進來了。
聞起來像久放的食用油，而不是烘香加鹹香。
真的受潮的袋子出現霉或霉味。
tips: 買之前先看包裝上的有效日期，那是你唯一的時間軸。
開封後把袋口夾緊或倒進氣密盒；有鹽的軟得特別快。
整盤端出去前，先從袋子不同位置剝幾顆確認。

faq.q: 帶殼鹹葵瓜子可以放多久？
faq.a: 沒有公布固定期限。請以包裝上的有效日期為準，並且密封放在陰涼、乾燥、避光處。
會。烤過的種子長時間放在室溫下就會油耗，這也是為什麼包裝上的日期值得當一回事。
殼上的鹽把潮濕空氣中的水吸了過來。請確實重新密封，或改放氣密盒。
